title: Standard Chinese SVO & Time/Place Order
explanation: Mandarin places Time and Place BEFORE the verb: Subject + Time + Place + Verb + Object.
example: 我今天在图书馆学习中文。
example_translation: Today I study Chinese at the library.

title: Aspect & Change-of-State Particle 了 (le)
explanation: Placed right after a verb to mark a completed action, or at the end of a sentence to indicate a new situation.
example: 我已经吃了早饭。
example_translation: I have already eaten breakfast.

title: Structural Particles 的 / 地 / 得
explanation: 的 modifies nouns (我的书), 地 turns adjectives into adverbs before verbs (认真地学), and 得 introduces degree complements after verbs (说得很好).
example: 他高兴地说得很快。
example_translation: He happily spoke very fast.

title: Negation: 不 (bù) vs. 没 (méi)
explanation: Use 不 to negate present, future, or habitual actions and adjectives; use 没 / 没有 to negate past actions or 有 (possession).
example: 我昨天没去，今天也不去。
example_translation: I did not go yesterday, and I am not going today either.

title: Question & Modal Particles 吗 / 呢 / 吧
explanation: 吗 turns a statement into a yes/no question; 呢 asks bounce-back questions ("and you?"); 吧 softens suggestions or seeks agreement.
example: 我们一起去学习吧！
example_translation: Let’s go study together!

title: Experiential Particle 过 (guò)
explanation: Placed immediately after a verb (Verb + 过) to express having experienced something at least once in the past.
example: 我去过北京两次。
example_translation: I have been to Beijing twice.

title: Continuous State Particle 着 (zhe)
explanation: Verb + 着 indicates an ongoing state or posture (e.g., 门开着 — the door is open).
example: 墙上挂着一张地图。
example_translation: A map is hanging on the wall.

title: Comparison Structure with 比 (bǐ)
explanation: A + 比 + B + Adjective (+ degree) compares two things. Never put 很 directly before the adjective in a 比 sentence.
example: 今天比昨天冷一点儿。
example_translation: Today is a little colder than yesterday.

title: The 把 (bǎ) Disposal Construction
explanation: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + Result/Complement highlights how a definite object is affected, moved, or handled.
example: 请把作业放在桌子上。
example_translation: Please put the homework on the desk.

title: Passive Voice with 被 (bèi)
explanation: Receiver + 被 (+ Agent) + Verb + Result expresses passive actions where something happens to the subject.
example: 我的词典被同学借走了。
example_translation: My dictionary was borrowed by a classmate.

title: Cause & Effect: 因为…所以…
explanation: Pairs 因为 (because) in the cause clause with 所以 (therefore) in the result clause.
example: 因为下雨，所以我们留在家里。
example_translation: Because it rained, we stayed home.

title: Concession: 虽然…但是…
explanation: 虽然 (although) always pairs with 但是 / 可是 (but) in Mandarin — unlike English, both conjunctions appear together.
example: 虽然汉字很难，但是很有意思。
example_translation: Although Chinese characters are hard, they are very interesting.

title: Progressive Structure: 不但…而且…
explanation: Means "not only... but also...". Keep不但 after the subject if both clauses share the same subject.
example: 她不但会说英语，而且会说中文。
example_translation: She speaks not only English, but also Chinese.

title: Gradual Change: 越来越 + Adj/Mental Verb
explanation: Expresses "more and more..." over time. Do not add 很 with 越来越.
example: 你的发音越来越标准了。
example_translation: Your pronunciation is getting more and more accurate.

title: English SVO Order & Subject–Verb Agreement
explanation: Standard English follows Subject + Verb + Object. In the present simple, 3rd-person singular subjects (he/she/it) require -s/-es on the verb.
example: She studies vocabulary every morning.
example_translation: সে প্রতিদিন সকালে শব্দভাণ্ডার পড়ে।

title: Articles: a / an / the
explanation: Use "a" before consonant sounds, "an" before vowel sounds for non-specific singular countable nouns, and "the" when the listener knows which specific item is meant.
example: I bought a book. The book is very helpful.

title: Perfect Aspect (have / has / had + Past Participle)
explanation: Links past actions to the present (have/has + V3) or an earlier past moment (had + V3). Avoid pairing present perfect with specific past times like "yesterday".
example: I have already finished my assignment.

title: Modal Verbs + Base Infinitive
explanation: Modal verbs (can, could, should, must, might, would) are always followed directly by the base verb without "to" or "-s".
example: You should practice speaking every day.

title: Conditional Clauses (If / Unless)
explanation: First conditional (If + present simple, will + verb) expresses real future possibilities; second conditional (If + past simple, would + verb) expresses hypothetical situations.
example: If you review daily, you will remember more words.

title: Prepositions of Time & Place (in / on / at)
explanation: Use "at" for exact times/points (at 7 PM, at school), "on" for days/dates/surfaces (on Monday, on the desk), and "in" for months/years/enclosed spaces (in July, in Dhaka).
example: Our exam starts at 9:00 AM on Monday.

title: Contrast Connectors: Although vs. Despite / However
explanation: "Although" is followed by a full Subject + Verb clause; "despite / in spite of" is followed by a noun or -ing gerund.
example: Although it was late, he kept studying.

title: Auxiliary Do / Does / Did in Questions & Negatives
explanation: When forming questions or negatives with do/does/did, keep the main verb in its base form (e.g., "Did she go?" — never "Did she went?").
example: Does he understand this grammar rule?

title: Bangla SOV Word Order
explanation: Bangla places the conjugated verb at the end of the sentence: Subject (কর্তা) + Object (কর্ম) + Verb (ক্রিয়া).
example: আমি প্রতিদিন নতুন শব্দ শিখি।
example_translation: I learn new words every day.

title: Pronoun Honorific Levels & Verb Agreement
explanation: Bangla has 3 second-person registers that require matching verb endings: আপনি (formal: করেন/যান), তুমি (familiar: করো/যাও), and তুই (intimate: করিস/যাস).
example: আপনি কেমন আছেন? / তুমি কেমন আছো?
example_translation: How are you? (formal / familiar)

title: Bangla Negation: না vs. নি vs. নয়
explanation: Place না after the verb for present/future negation, নি (with present-form stem) for past/perfect negation, and নয়/নন to negate identity ("is not").
example: আমি আজ যাইনি, কালও যাবো না।
example_translation: I did not go today, and I will not go tomorrow either.

title: Definite Classifiers (-টা / -টি / -জন)
explanation: Attaching -টা or -টি to a noun (বইটি = the book) or -জন for people (একজন শিক্ষক = a teacher) marks definiteness or counting.
example: বইটি খুব উপকারী।
example_translation: The book is very useful.

title: Case Endings (বিভক্তি) & Postpositions (অনুসর্গ)
explanation: Instead of prepositions before nouns, Bangla attaches suffixes (-কে object, -র/-এর possessive, -তে/-য় locative) and places postpositions (জন্য, থেকে, সাথে) after the possessive noun.
example: শিক্ষকের সাথে কথা বলুন।
example_translation: Speak with the teacher.

title: Conditional Sentences: যদি … তাহলে …
explanation: Pairs যদি (if) at the start of the condition clause with তাহলে / তবে (then) at the start of the result clause.
example: যদি নিয়মিত পড়ো, তাহলে ভালো ফল করবে।
example_translation: If you study regularly, you will do well.
